1001.name: Red Door Family Shelter
1001.intakeNotes: Family shelter — call Red Door or Central Intake (416-338-4766 / 311) for referral. Spaces are limited.
requirements: Homeless families, including refugee families and women with children fleeing abuse
Confirm current address and program site when referred — listings can change
1001.transit: Depends on active program site; ask intake for the best TTC route
1001.summary: Red Door supports families and women with children who need emergency shelter, including people fleeing domestic abuse and some newcomer families.

1008.name: TSSS Seaton House
1008.intakeNotes: City-operated Seaton House programs (including harm-reduction Annex services). Call Central Intake at 416-338-4766 or 311 for referral to available men’s beds.
requirements: Primarily men; some programs support people with complex mental health or substance-use needs
Referral through Central Intake is the usual path
1008.transit: George Street near Dundas / Sherbourne; bus and streetcar nearby
1008.summary: Seaton House is a large City-operated men’s shelter site with specialized programs, including harm-reduction supports. Start with Central Intake for a bed tonight.

1022.name: Good Shepherd Centre
1022.intakeNotes: Overnight shelter for men. Call the centre or Central Intake (416-338-4766) for referral and hours.
requirements: Homeless or disadvantaged men 18 and older
Ask about ID and belongings when you call
1022.transit: Queen streetcar near Queen and Parliament / Sherbourne
1022.summary: Good Shepherd Centre on Queen Street East provides overnight shelter and supports for men experiencing homelessness.

1026.name: Covenant House Gerrard St E
1026.intakeNotes: Call intake or visit Covenant House for screening. Crisis line also available at 1-800-435-7308. Also call City Central Intake at 416-338-4766 for shelter referral.
requirements: Serves youth ages 16–24
Wheelchair access available — call for details
Documents may vary; ask intake what to bring
1026.transit: Near Dundas Station / Yonge–Dundas area; streetcar and subway nearby
1026.summary: Youth emergency shelter on Gerrard Street East with food, clothing, medical care, counselling, and help toward housing, school, and work. Open to young people including survivors of trafficking or sexual exploitation.

1037.name: SA Gateway
1037.intakeNotes: Men’s hostel with drop-in supports. Call Gateway or Central Intake (416-338-4766) for shelter beds.
requirements: Shelter program for men 21+
Drop-in may have separate hours and age rules — ask when you call
1037.transit: Near Jarvis and Queen; streetcar nearby
1037.summary: Salvation Army Gateway on Jarvis Street offers men’s hostel beds and drop-in supports for people who are homeless or under-housed.

1045.name: Street Haven
1045.intakeNotes: Emergency hostel for women in crisis. Call the shelter or City Central Intake (416-338-4766) for bed availability and referral.
requirements: Single women 16+ in crisis, including homelessness, violence, addiction, or mental-health challenges
Ask staff about ID and belongings rules
1045.transit: Near Dundas / Sherbourne area; TTC bus and streetcar nearby
1045.summary: Women’s emergency hostel on Pembroke Street for people facing homelessness, violence, trauma, or addiction. Offers a place to stay and crisis supports.

1048.name: SVDP Mary's Home
1048.intakeNotes: Emergency shelter for single homeless women. Call ahead or use Central Intake (416-338-4766) to check space.
requirements: Single homeless women 16 and older
Confirm current intake process by phone
1048.transit: Near Yonge–Dundas / Gerrard; subway and streetcar nearby
1048.summary: St. Vincent de Paul Mary’s Home is an emergency shelter for single homeless women on Gerrard Street East.

1057.name: Maxwell Meighen Centre
1057.intakeNotes: Salvation Army men’s hostel. Call the site or Central Intake (416-338-4766) about beds and intake.
requirements: Men 18+ who can manage stairs / ambulatory programs — confirm accessibility needs by phone
Bring ID if you have it
1057.transit: Near Sherbourne and Queen; streetcar and bus routes nearby
1057.summary: Salvation Army Maxwell Meighen Centre is a men’s hostel on Sherbourne Street with emergency overnight beds.

1059.name: Sojourn House Ontario St
1059.intakeNotes: Shelter for refugees and refugee claimants (singles and families). Call Sojourn House extensions for intake, or Central Intake (416-338-4766).
requirements: Refugees / refugee claimants — singles and families
Ask which documents help with intake
1059.transit: Near Queen and Ontario / downtown east; streetcar nearby
1059.summary: Sojourn House on Ontario Street provides emergency shelter and support for refugees and refugee claimants, including single people and families.

1070.name: TSSS Birkdale Residence
1070.intakeNotes: City family residence in Scarborough. Call Central Intake (416-338-4766) or 311 for referral — do not assume walk-in beds.
requirements: Homeless women with children / family households — confirm eligibility with intake
Referral-based placement
1070.transit: Near Ellesmere Road in Scarborough; TTC bus connections
1070.summary: Birkdale Residence is a City shelter program for families. Placement normally goes through Central Intake.
